meta.title: Kanban
meta.description: A multi-container drag-and-drop board. Drag cards within and between columns, drag columns to reorder, with a virtual state machine that shows placeholders live during drag — committed once on drop.

blocks.content: Single-container drag-and-drop is solved. Multi-container isn't. When a card crosses a column boundary, dnd-kit's default collision detection breaks. The placeholder needs to appear in the target column before the drop. The state needs to reflect mid-drag positions for visual feedback without mutating your actual data. Rollback on cancel needs to be clean.

KanbanRoot owns a virtual columns state that tracks in-drag positions. On every onDragOver event it updates this state — the placeholder appears live, the source column gap closes, the target column opens. On drop it commits once via onColumnsChange. On cancel it rolls back to the pre-drag snapshot. Your data only changes when the user completes a drag.

blocks.title: The virtual state machine
blocks.content: KanbanRoot keeps dragColumns as local state — a copy of your columns that gets mutated on every onDragOver. This is what drives the live placeholder. On onDragEnd it calls onColumnsChange(dragColumns) to commit. On onDragCancel it resets from a snapshot taken at onDragStart. Your columns prop never changes until drop.
A full sprint board with priority badges, assignee avatars, and due dates. Drag any card between columns or within a column. Drag a column header to reorder columns.
Kanban uses dnd-kit, which you already have installed if you're using the Sortable system.

blocks.content: Extend KanbanCardBase and KanbanColumnBase with your domain fields, then pass your columns to KanbanRoot with a renderCard function. KanbanBoard reads from context and renders everything.

blocks.title: renderCard is used in two places
blocks.content: The same renderCard function renders cards in their columns AND in the DragOverlay ghost. The meta.isOverlay flag lets you style the ghost differently — a slightly lifted shadow, bolder border, or reduced opacity on the original slot via meta.isDragging.
All visual surfaces are render props on KanbanRoot. Column headers double as drag handles for column reordering — whatever you pass to renderColumnHeader becomes the drag trigger.

blocks.content: Used internally by KanbanBoard. Expose it if you need to build a custom board layout. Each column is both useSortable (for column reordering) and useDroppable (to accept cards when empty).
Used internally by KanbanColumn. Each card is useSortable with data.type = 'card'. The renderCard function from context fills the content.
Call useKanban() anywhere inside KanbanRoot to build custom panels, sidebars, or controls that read or reflect board state.
